title: Chronic idiopathic constipation (adult)
subject: gastroenterology
summary: Exclude alarm features and secondary causes, then step up: fibre, polyethylene glycol (strong recommendation), magnesium oxide or lactulose, stimulant laxatives (bisacodyl or sodium picosulfate, senna), and for refractory cases linaclotide, plecanatide, lubiprostone or prucalopride. Test for a defecatory disorder if laxatives fail.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Rome IV: 2 or more of straining, hard or lumpy stools, incomplete evacuation, sense of blockage, or manual manoeuvres (each in over a quarter of defecations), or under 3 spontaneous bowel movements a week; for 3 months, onset 6 months or more earlier, IBS criteria not met.

Alarm features needing colonoscopy or referral: rectal bleeding, iron deficiency anaemia, unexplained weight loss, new onset or sudden change after age 50, family history of colorectal cancer or IBD, positive faecal immunochemical test, or an abdominal or rectal mass.

Secondary causes: drugs (opioids, anticholinergics, tricyclics, calcium channel blockers, iron, calcium, aluminium antacids), hypothyroidism, hypercalcaemia, diabetes, Parkinson disease, pregnancy, and immobility.
Symptoms of a defecatory (evacuation) disorder: prolonged straining, digital assistance, incomplete evacuation despite soft stool.

sections.title: Investigations
items: History of diet, fluids, medicines and toilet habits, and a digital rectal examination (look for impaction, anal fissure, rectocele and paradoxical anal contraction on straining).
Full blood count. Thyroid function, calcium and glucose when clinically suggested.
Colonoscopy only for alarm features or when due for colorectal cancer screening.
Failure of an adequate laxative trial: anorectal manometry with balloon expulsion test to diagnose dyssynergic defecation (treated with biofeedback, not more laxatives).

sections.title: Step 1: fibre and osmotic laxatives
items: Fibre supplement (psyllium preferred) with adequate fluid, increased gradually over weeks to limit bloating (conditional recommendation).
Polyethylene glycol (strong recommendation): first-line laxative if fibre is insufficient or not tolerated; can be used long term.
Magnesium oxide or lactulose are alternatives (conditional recommendations). Avoid magnesium in renal impairment (hypermagnesaemia); lactulose often causes bloating and flatulence.
Review and stop constipating drugs where possible.

sections.title: Step 2: stimulant laxatives
items: Bisacodyl or sodium picosulfate (strong recommendation) for short-term use or as rescue therapy on top of an osmotic laxative.
Senna is a reasonable option (conditional recommendation).
Abdominal cramping and diarrhoea are the main adverse effects of stimulant laxatives; titrate to the lowest effective dose.

sections.title: Step 3: prescription agents for refractory CIC
items: Secretagogues: linaclotide or plecanatide (strong recommendations) or lubiprostone (conditional). Diarrhoea is the main adverse effect of linaclotide and plecanatide; nausea is common with lubiprostone.
Prucalopride, a 5-HT4 agonist (strong recommendation); reduce the dose in severe renal impairment.
Choose among these by shared decision making on cost, availability, adverse effects and patient preference.
Before escalating further, exclude a defecatory disorder with anorectal testing.

sections.title: Special groups
items: Older adults: check for faecal impaction (overflow diarrhoea), immobility and constipating drugs; use magnesium cautiously with reduced renal function.
Opioid-induced constipation: start a laxative with the opioid; peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonists are an option if laxatives fail (separate protocol).
Pregnancy: fibre, polyethylene glycol and lactulose are commonly used first-line options.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Missing colorectal cancer in new-onset constipation after 50 or with alarm features.
Escalating laxatives in dyssynergic defecation instead of referring for biofeedback.
Magnesium laxatives in chronic kidney disease.
Stopping effective therapy too early: chronic constipation usually needs maintenance treatment.

drugs.name: Psyllium (ispaghula) husk
drugs.dose: About 5 g orally once or twice daily with a full glass of water, increased gradually
drugs.notes: Take with adequate fluid; bloating early on.

drugs.name: Polyethylene glycol 3350 (macrogol)
drugs.dose: 17 g orally once daily dissolved in about 240 mL of fluid, titrate to response

drugs.name: Magnesium oxide
drugs.dose: 400 to 500 mg orally daily, titrate to response

drugs.name: Lactulose
drugs.dose: 15 mL (about 10 g) orally once or twice daily, adjusted to response

drugs.name: Bisacodyl
drugs.notes: Short term or rescue; abdominal cramps.

drugs.name: Linaclotide
drugs.dose: 145 mcg orally once daily (72 mcg if not tolerated), at least 30 minutes before the first meal
drugs.notes: Diarrhoea is the main adverse effect.

drugs.name: Prucalopride
drugs.dose: 2 mg orally once daily; 1 mg once daily if eGFR below 30 mL/min

drugs.name: Lubiprostone
drugs.dose: 24 mcg orally twice daily with food
